draft.text: You came to the doctor because you were referred from the ER for esophagitis.
You had chest pain three months ago that lasted four days and went away.
You also had trouble swallowing during that time.
You are currently feeling fine and have no symptoms of esophagitis or chest pain now.
Tests done in the ER, like an EKG and blood tests, did not find any heart problems.
Your doctor thought the issue might be related to your stomach or esophagus instead of your heart.
You have a history of esophagitis, but it has not returned since three months ago.
Your doctor believes the chest pain you had was not related to your heart, based on the tests.
You will keep an eye on your symptoms and may consider an upper endoscopy in the future if you have more symptoms.
You are currently doing well, but you wanted reassurance that there are no other issues.

unverified_summary.text: You came to the doctor because you had chest pain and trouble swallowing a few months ago.
This happened near your breastbone and lasted about four days.
You are now feeling better and have not had any symptoms since the initial episode.
You do not smoke or drink alcohol, and you are trying to lose weight.
You have a history of esophagitis, which is inflammation of the esophagus.
Your chest pain and swallowing issues have resolved, and you are currently without symptoms.
You should keep an eye on your symptoms.
If you experience any new issues, you may consider an upper endoscopy in the future.
No specific follow-up plan was discussed at this time.
